purpose: find real problems worth solving and test the idea cheaply before committing to build it
entry_criteria: A target user group or problem area is named
The team has time for short experiments
procedure: Write the problem hypotheses as who has the problem, what happens, and why it matters.
Interview users about past behavior, not opinions about your idea, and record what they say.
Rank problems by frequency, pain and willingness to change, using evidence from the interviews.
For the best problem, run the cheapest test of a solution: prototype, concierge version or landing page.
Set the success threshold before the test, then judge by it.
Decide to proceed, change direction or stop, and record the evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Success threshold was set before the test
Decision is based on the threshold
Stopping is a valid recorded outcome

validation.check: confirm the success threshold was written before the experiment started
count interviews supporting each ranked problem

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Eight interviews show that small teams re-enter data between two tools weekly. A concierge version run by hand for five teams meets the pre-set threshold of three repeat uses, so the idea proceeds to planning.
